newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH NFI 3 WANTS TO FOCUS ON 50 FIRMS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH NFI 3 WANTS TO FOCUS ON 50 FIRMS.

text.p: Polish National Investment Fund No 3 of Poland's mass privatisation scheme wants to concentrate on about 50 companies, mainly from the construction sector by year 2000, a member of the NFI's management said on Tuesday.
"After three years we plan to have assets of the fund concentrated in about 50 firms," Janusz Koczyk told a news conference.

He said by the end of 2000 the 50 companies from the fund's current portfolio and bought later would make two thirds of its portfolio. He added the fund wanted to keep them in the portfolio for a period of between three and five years.
Under Poland's mass privatisation programme, 15 NFIs were given control of stakes of over 60 percent in more than 500 medium-sized companies.
Each fund, run by international managers, was given a leading, 33 percent stake in more than 30 companies and small equity stakes in the remaining firms.

From May 12, the 26 million Poles who bought participation units in the scheme have been entitled to exchange them for 15 shares, one in each fund, which start trading on the Warsaw bourse on June 12.
